summary: vary_cache_key does not type-check Mapping values; bytes/other non-str values pass through silently. Caller-trust boundary, not a parser defect.
vary_cache_key does not type-check Mapping keys; Mapping[int, str] would raise on .lower(). Type signature already advertises Mapping[str, str].
Parser does not cap input length; 1 GiB input allocates ~1 GiB. Real HTTP servers cap headers upstream (8-16 KiB), so not exploitable in production.
CLI subprocess surface runs at 27.7 iters/s vs ~3K for in-process surfaces. Structural bottleneck is subprocess.run; coverage is still meaningful (4,500 distinct invocations).
Type-errors surface runs at ~922K iters/s because SUT type-checks and rejects in O(1) per call. Coverage is exhaustive across the 21+8 input pool.
1 MiB-cap large inputs complete inside the 10 s subprocess timeout without OOM. Confirms parse_vary is O(N) memory, not superlinear.
